To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Middle Cambrian carbonate platform in the southern Appalachains evolved from a gently sloping ramp to a steeply dipping rimmed platform; (2) this transition was from a carbonate ramp to a rimed platform and (3) the transition was from a shallow water carbonate ramp to a deep water rimed platform.

the Middle and Late Cambrian strata of the southern Appalachian passive margin consist of a series of six carbonate-shale sequences that record a gradual transition from a carbonate ramp to a rim platform.
the Maryville Limestones are a prograding carbonate platform that evolved from a gently dipping ramp to a rim with steeper slopes, with the progradation of the platform being toward the craton.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Maryville L limestone (Middle Cambrian, Conasauga Group, southern Appalachians) is a composite sequence consisting of two subsequences, each of which is a combination of aggradaitional, retrogradaitional, and prograditional units.
the Maryville L limestone represents a transition from an intrashelf carbonate ramp to a rim margin.

the Conasauga Group is the result of the gradual progradation of the carbonate platform from the craton into the intrashelf basin, and the gradual evolution from a gently sloping ramp-like platform to a rimmed-platform setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Conasauga Group is a composite, composite depositional sequence.
the Maryville sequence is composed of two subsequences, which are separated by an exposure surface and drowning unconformity.
the Conasauga Group is the product of a complex interplay between eustasy, sedimentation rate, and subsidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

sequence boundaries in carbonate ramp to rim platforms may be difficult to recognize because of their gradational nature and because they may not separate rocks deposited during different environmental regimes.
the Maryville L. represents a gradual ramp to rimmed-platform transition that is not a classic sequence boundary.
the sequence stratigraphic framework of the Maryville is the product of a combination of tectonic subsidence and eustasy, with sediment supply playing a secondary role.
